planting.note: Pot divisions or offsets into a mineral-poor, well-drained mix such as long-fiber sphagnum and perlite, and keep the central leaf tank topped up with rainwater or distilled water year-round.

directions: Brocchinia reducta grows on the open, fire-swept tepui savannas of the Venezuelan Gran Sabana and adjoining Guyana, where its tight rosette of yellowish-green, waxy leaves forms a water-filled central tank. The inner leaf surface is coated with a loose, powdery wax that makes it treacherously slick for crawling insects, which slide down into the standing water and are broken down by resident bacteria rather than digestive enzymes, one of the few confirmed cases of carnivory in the bromeliad family. In cultivation it is grown much like Heliamphora, in a bright, humid setting with a mineral-poor, well-drained mix and the central tank kept filled with rainwater or distilled water. Established plants tolerate the periodic savanna fires of their native habitat and are remarkably tough once acclimated, slowly producing basal offsets that can be divided to start new plants.
